From: Sarah Kaplan <sarah@kaplanlabs.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: High p99 + 503s during morning batch run (Kaplan)

Hi Irene —

We started a large ingestion job this morning (approx 120k requests over 30m) and saw long tails: p95 was ok, but p99 jumped to ~4.8s for a sustained 10-minute window and ~6% 503/error rate. This impacted our scoring pipeline and caused downstream backpressure. Attached are logs and a short trace (kaplan-requests-20270321.log).

Quick details:
- Region: us-west1
- Model: gpt-open-13b (hosted) pinned v1.4
- Observed behavior: sudden request queuing, many requests stalled waiting for concurrency slots; some requests timed out and returned 503 after 30s

We need an urgent ops runbook — can you advise immediate mitigations and whether this looks like an internal throttling/concurrency cap issue vs model slowdown?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Kaplan
Ops Lead, Kaplan Labs

Subject: Re: High p99 + 503s during morning batch run (Kaplan)

Sarah —

Thanks for the quick report and logs. We're pulling an immediate triage channel. Initial ask: can you confirm if the traffic was all to a single route/model key or sharded across multiple routes? Also any spike in input sequence length distribution?

Planned short-term actions (30–90m):
- Temporary increase per-tenant concurrency cap for Kaplan by +50% (if infra allows)
- Enable fallback to the smaller gpt-open-6b model for overflow (non-blocking)
- Increase request timeout to 45s for in-flight requests to reduce 503 churn while we stabilize

I'll run the above with Marissa and Markus on-call; Vivek — can you validate capacity headroom in us-west1 and whether autoscaler is suppressed?

I'll follow up with a brief runbook and link to the change play (will attach runbook_kaplan_v1.pdf).

— Irene

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Sarah Kaplan <sarah@kaplanlabs.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High p99 + 503s during morning batch run (Kaplan)

Irene / team —

I pulled the service metrics and can confirm a clear queue-depth spike at the model front-end correlating with the window Sarah mentioned. Key observations:
- Concurrency cap for Kaplan was set to 120 concurrent tokens/requests; sustained bursts hit 115–120, which triggered request queuing in the per-tenant queue layer.
- During the spike, several requests experienced KV cache misses (higher latency on first token generation), which amplified service times and created head-of-line blocking.
- Autoscaler did not kick immediately because the aggregate cluster utilization was ~78%, and our scale threshold is conservative to avoid flapping.

Immediate mitigation I applied (09:38):
1) Raised Kaplan concurrency cap to 180 (temporary, until 12:00 PDT)
2) Enabled overflow routing to gpt-open-6b for non-critical routes (opt-in by client)
3) Warmed KV cache for Kaplan's most common prefixes and pre-seeded a subset of hot keys

Preliminary impact: p99 dropped from ~4.8s to ~1.1s within 6 minutes; error rate reduced to ~0.9%. We should keep monitoring.

Follow-ups needed:
- Policy: adjust per-tenant concurrency cap heuristics for batch workloads vs interactive.
- Short-term: lower autoscaler threshold slightly for the next 48 hours for the affected pool.
- Long-term: change backpressure algorithm to favor short-running requests and prevent head-of-line blocking (engineering ticket INF-7823).

— Markus
Markus Klein
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
